questions.question: How does Jim feel when he wakes up? Can you remember what was wrong for him?
questions.explanation: This question helps children show they understand how someone can feel grumpy even if nothing is really wrong, making the concept of 'bad moods for no reason' relatable.

questions.question: What do Jim’s friends, like Norman and Marabou, do when they notice Jim is grumpy?
questions.explanation: This question invites children to discuss how friends notice and show curiosity about how others feel, reinforcing the importance of paying attention to others’ feelings.

questions.question: Do you think Jim feels better when he tries smiling or loosening up, even though his friends tell him to?
questions.explanation: Helps children think about the difference between pretending to feel happy and actually feeling happy, connecting to their own experiences.

questions.question: When the animals suggest lots of fun things to cheer Jim up, does it work? What does Jim do instead?
questions.explanation: Shows kids that sometimes, when you feel down, doing fun things is not always what you need, helping them recognize different ways to handle emotions.

questions.question: Has there been a day when you felt grumpy, even if other people tried to cheer you up?
questions.explanation: Encourages children to connect the story to their own lives, normalizing the feeling of being grumpy and not always wanting to join in.

questions.question: What did Jim do after he shouted at everyone? How did he feel?
questions.explanation: Helps children see how handling big feelings can sometimes lead to saying or doing things you didn’t mean, and how it’s okay to feel sorry afterwards.

questions.question: Why do you think Jim started to feel a little better when he was with his friend Norman at the end?
questions.explanation: Gets children thinking about the power of friendship and how just being with someone can help you feel better, even if you are still grumpy.

questions.question: What would you do if you saw a friend looking sad or grumpy? What could you say to them?
questions.explanation: This question helps children practice empathy and caring behavior, learning ways to support friends who feel down.

questions.question: Is it okay to feel grumpy sometimes? Why or why not?
questions.explanation: Offers a chance to summarize and generalize the moral lesson in simple terms, helping children accept their own and others' feelings.

moral: It's okay to feel grumpy sometimes, and you don't always have to pretend you feel happy. Talking about your feelings or just having a friend with you can help you feel better.
learning_objectives: Children will be able to identify and name feelings like grumpy, happy, and sad.
Children will learn that it's okay to feel grumpy sometimes and you don't always have to pretend to be happy.
Children will learn simple ways to support friends who feel sad or grumpy.
Children will practice sharing their own feelings and talking about what makes them feel better.
